title: acks=all: the write is acknowledged once enough replicas have it
caption: Replication factor 3, min.insync.replicas = 2. Losing any one broker loses no acknowledged record.

messages.label: produce batch (acks=all)
messages.note: With acks=1 the leader would answer right here, and a leader crash in the next millisecond loses the batch.

messages.label: fetch → copy batch
messages.note: Followers pull from the leader, just like consumers do.

messages.label: all in-sync replicas have it
messages.note: acks=all waits for every replica in the ISR. min.insync.replicas = 2 is a floor: if fewer than 2 are in sync, the leader refuses the write instead of acking it.

messages.label: ack
messages.note: This costs a few ms more than acks=1.

messages.label: broker 1 dies
messages.note: A follower from the in-sync set becomes leader. It has the batch, so nothing acknowledged is lost.

scenarios.name: acks=1: leader dies
scenarios.summary: With acks=1 the producer is told 'done' before any follower has the batch. If the leader dies right then, an acknowledged write disappears.

messages.label: ack
messages.note: The leader answers as soon as the batch is on its own disk.

messages.label: broker 1 dies
messages.note: Followers haven't fetched the batch yet.

messages.label: elected leader, no batch
messages.note: Broker 2 takes over without the record. The producer was told it was written: silent data loss.

scenarios.name: ISR shrinks
scenarios.summary: A follower that falls behind is dropped from the ISR, and acks=all waits only for the rest. Below min.insync.replicas the leader refuses writes rather than risk losing them.

messages.label: slow disk, falls behind
messages.note: After replica.lag.time.max (30 s) without catching up, broker 3 leaves the ISR: now {1, 2}.

messages.label: fetch → copy batch
messages.note: All in-sync replicas (1 and 2) have it: 2 ≥ min.insync.replicas.

messages.label: ack
messages.note: Still durable against one more broker loss.

messages.label: NotEnoughReplicas
messages.note: If broker 2 drops out too, the ISR is {1}: fewer than 2, so writes are refused. Durability over availability.

scenarios.name: Leader dies before ack
scenarios.summary: The batch was replicated but the ack never arrived, so the producer retries on the new leader. An idempotent producer turns that retry into a no-op instead of a duplicate.

messages.label: retry batch, seq 41
messages.note: Timeout, metadata refresh: broker 2 is the new leader, so the producer resends the batch to it.

messages.label: ack (duplicate dropped)
messages.note: Same producer id and sequence number: broker 2 recognises the retry and doesn't append the batch twice.
